flashcard_questions.q: What is meant by static electricity?
flashcard_questions.a: A build-up of charge on the surface of an object, caused by electrons transferring through friction.

flashcard_questions.q: Which particle moves when two materials are charged by rubbing?
What overall charge is left on a material that has lost electrons?
What overall charge is left on a material that has gained extra electrons?
When a polythene rod is rubbed with a woollen cloth, which way do the electrons move?
flashcard_questions.a: From the wool onto the rod.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does static charge build up on insulators but not on conductors?
flashcard_questions.a: A conductor lets the transferred electrons flow away, while an insulator holds them on its surface.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens when two objects carrying the same type of charge are brought close?
Why can a charged rod attract small pieces of uncharged paper?
flashcard_questions.a: It rearranges the surface electrons on the paper — a process called electrostatic induction.

flashcard_questions.q: What charge builds up on the dome of a Van de Graaff generator?
flashcard_questions.a: A large positive charge, because the belt carries electrons away from the dome.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does a person's hair stand on end when they touch a Van de Graaff dome?
flashcard_questions.a: Each strand gains the same charge, so the hairs repel one another.

flashcard_questions.q: What is sparking between a charged object and the earth?
flashcard_questions.a: A sudden flow of charge through the air, caused by a large potential difference.

flashcard_questions.q: How does earthing stop a dangerous build-up of static charge?
flashcard_questions.a: A conductor gives the electrons a safe path to flow to or from the ground.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is a static build-up dangerous when a vehicle is being refuelled?
flashcard_questions.a: A spark near the fuel vapour could start a fire or an explosion.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is the paint given the opposite charge to the object in electrostatic spray painting?
flashcard_questions.a: The droplets are attracted evenly to the surface, giving a smooth coat with less waste.

flashcard_questions.q: Which way do electric field lines point around a positive charge?
flashcard_questions.a: Away from it, in the direction a positive charge would move.
